title: Limits on the Second Amendment Right
short: Heller (2008) called longstanding prohibitions presumptively lawful (possession by felons and the mentally ill, carrying in sensitive places, conditions on commercial sale) and protected arms in common use, not dangerous and unusual ones; Caetano v. Massachusetts (2016) applied Heller to stun guns; since 2022 the Court has judged gun laws by the Nation's historical tradition of firearm regulation rather than by tiers of scrutiny.
trouble: Students think Heller struck down all gun laws, or that it let governments ban any weapon. It named longstanding regulations as presumptively lawful and protected arms in common use.

blocks.html: Note: This is an educational course, not legal advice.

Heller and McDonald held that the Second Amendment protects an individual right that binds every level of government. They also said the right "is not unlimited." This topic looks at the limits the Court itself described: which people, which places and which weapons.

laws "forbidding the carrying of firearms in sensitive places such as schools and government buildings" are also presumptively lawful

opts.name: Caetano v. Massachusetts
opts.q: May a state ban stun guns because they did not exist at the founding and are not military weapons?
opts.holding: Those reasons contradict Heller; the Second Amendment extends to bearable arms not in existence at the founding.
opts.facts: Jaime Caetano kept a stun gun for protection after a former boyfriend had attacked her. She was convicted under a Massachusetts law banning stun guns. The state's highest court upheld the conviction, reasoning that stun guns did not exist when the amendment was adopted and were not the kind of weapon a militia would use.
opts.reasoning: In a short unsigned opinion, the Court said each of those reasons contradicted Heller: the amendment reaches arms that did not exist at the founding, and Heller rejected the idea that only arms useful in war are protected. It sent the case back. Justice Alito, joined by Justice Thomas, would have gone further and reversed the conviction outright.

blocks.html: Heller's list of "presumptively lawful" measures was short and came without a full explanation, and the Court said it was giving examples, not an exhaustive list. After 2008 many lower courts used a two-step method: they asked whether a law touched conduct the amendment protects, and if so applied intermediate or strict scrutiny. Since 2022 the Court has judged gun laws by the Nation's historical tradition of firearm regulation rather than by these tiers. Heller's majority had already rejected Justice Breyer's proposal to weigh a gun law's benefits against its burdens case by case. Supporters of that choice say an enumerated right should not depend on judges' views of its costs; critics say public safety must count and that history gives judges little guidance about modern weapons and places.

Heller called longstanding prohibitions presumptively lawful: possession by felons and the mentally ill, carrying in sensitive places, and conditions on commercial sale. The right covers arms in common use, not "dangerous and unusual" ones, and reaches arms invented after 1791 (Caetano v. Massachusetts (2016)).

blocks.title: A new kind of weapon
blocks.q: A state argues that a hand-held electronic device for self-defense is not protected because nothing like it existed in 1791. What did the Court say about that argument?
steps: Heller said the amendment extends to all bearable arms, even those not in existence at the founding.
Caetano v. Massachusetts (2016) applied that to stun guns and rejected the state court's reasoning.
Whether a particular ban survives depends on more than the weapon's age.
blocks.a: The argument fails: newness alone does not remove a weapon from the amendment.

blocks.title: A courthouse rule
blocks.q: A state bans carrying firearms inside courthouses. What did Heller say about laws like this?
steps: Heller listed laws "forbidding the carrying of firearms in sensitive places such as schools and government buildings" among presumptively lawful measures.
A courthouse is a government building.
blocks.a: Heller described such laws as presumptively lawful.

blocks.html: Thinking Heller struck down all gun laws, or that it let governments ban any weapon. It struck down a ban on handguns, the most popular arm for home defense, and it named longstanding regulations that remain presumptively lawful. Check: which people, which place, which weapon?
